extracted.intended_audience: organizations, universities, and industry teams in the U.S. national technology and industrial base preparing white papers or full proposals for ONR STAMP BAA N00014-23-S-B003
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit white papers or full proposals in response to ONR Broad Agency Announcement N00014-23-S-B003 (Science & Technology for Advanced Manufacturing Projects), complying with eligibility, format, content, and evaluation requirements and addressing program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission period and late proposal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: This announcement will remain open for approximately one (1) year from the date of publication, or until replaced by a successor BAA. Proposals may be submitted at any time during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government reserves the right not to review proposals submitted after 16 January 2024, or after a successor to this Long Range BAA is issued, whichever occurs first.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONR treatment of submitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR provides no funding for direct reimbursement of proposal development costs. Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this BAA will not be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR treats all proposals as sensitive competitive information and will disclose contents only for evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — national technology and industrial base
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is limited to persons and organizations that are part of the national technology and industrial base as defined in 10 U.S.C. § 4801. All responsible sources within that base from academia, industry, and the research community may submit proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HBCUs and Minority Institutions are encouraged to participate, but no portion of the BAA is set aside for them or any socio-economic group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible entities (FFRDCs, Navy labs, DOD labs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federally Funded Research & Development Centers (FFRDCs), Department of Energy National Laboratories, Navy laboratories, military universities, warfare centers, and other DoD and civilian agency laboratories are not eligible to receive awards under this BAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaming arrangements between FFRDCs and eligible principal Offerors are allowed if permitted by the sponsoring agreement; interested ineligible organizations should contact the ONR Technical POC.

rubrics_metrics.name: UARC eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: University Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs) are eligible to submit proposals unless precluded by their DoD UARC contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teams and data/software exchange expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams are encouraged and may submit proposals. Offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data, and other information in an integrated program with other contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated organizational capability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible organizations should have a demonstrated ability to bring government, industry, and academia together where joint development and commercialization can occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may include membership structures with defined royalty/licensing/revenue methods, mechanisms to ensure robust small/medium business participation, and coherent IP management and distributed facilities for R&D, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, and workforce development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted fundamental research policy
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR follows the USD(AT&L) definition of 'contracted fundamental research.' It includes research funded by Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) performed on-campus at a university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funded by Budget Activity 2 and NOT performed on-campus, or Budget Activities 3 or 4, do not meet the definition and may be subject to restrictions and DoD pre-publication review. Offerors should consult the ONR Technical POC to determine classification and must identify subcontracted fundamental research in proposals where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument type selection and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may take the form of contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, Technology Investment Agreements (TIAs), and Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research or prototype, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each instrument type has legal and policy implications (e.g., grants: no fee, no substantial involvement; cooperative agreements: substantial involvement; TIAs and OTAs: often expect ~50/50 cost share and other tailored terms). Offerors should anticipate instrument-specific terms and consult guides/links provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected under contracts and assistance awards and will not be used as a factor during merit review; however, the Government may consider voluntary cost sharing if proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIAs and OTAs may expect cost share (to the maximum extent practicable a 50/50 split). See 2 CFR 200.306 and FAR 35.003 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model contracts and grants caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Model contracts and grants are provided as examples; in the event of conflict, current FAR, DFARS, NMCARS, or ONR clauses will govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to example model contracts/grants are provided on the ONR website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier and SAM registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All Offerors must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid unique entity identifier, and maintain an active SAM registration while having an active Federal award or application under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal awarding agency may not make an award until an applicant has complied with UEI and SAM requirements; failure to comply can render an applicant unqualified for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper desirability and consult Technical POC
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers are frequently desired by ONR Program Officers; Offerors should consult the cognizant ONR Program Officer regarding desirability of White Paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Program Officer's information is a required field on the white paper cover sheet; FedConnect will not accept a white paper without the Cover Sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper Format: Paper Size – 8.5 x 11-inch; Margins – 1 inch; Spacing – single-spaced; Font – Times New Roman, 12 point; Page limit – 5 pages excluding cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When email submission is required, the white paper must be Microsoft Word 2016 or PDF compatible; email size limit 5 MB. ONR uses FedConnect for white paper submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper required content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include: Cover Page (MANDATORY); Technical Concept; Organizational Structure; Facilities; Future Department of Defense Relevance; Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page templates/cover sheet links provided; Technical Concept should describe proposed technology innovation, objective, technical approach, and risk areas; Organizational Structure should identify entities and relationships and key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal requirements reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposal Requirements are provided in Appendix 1 (Grants/Cooperative Agreements/TIAs) and Appendix 2 (Contracts/OTAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must follow the detailed Appendix instructions corresponding to their proposed instrument type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form — marking proprietary information
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions will be protected from unauthorized disclosure consistent with FAR Subpart 15.207. Offerors are expected to appropriately mark each page that contains proprietary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a non-proprietary Statement of Work; for data not to be disclosed outside the Government, mark the title page with the required legend and mark each restricted sheet with the specified legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-proprietary Statement of Work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For all proposals, a non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work must also be submitted. Do not put proprietary data or markings in or on the Statement of Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified proposals are submitted, an 'unclassified' SOW must accompany them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification handling
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers and Proposals are expected to be unclassified; classified proposals are permitted. If a classified proposal is submitted and selected, the resultant contract will be unclassified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified submissions require outer/inner envelope addressing and markings and must include an unclassified SOW with the classified package. Classified proposals shall be submitted to ONR's Document Control Unit as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal title guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles given to submissions should be descriptive of the work they cover and not merely a copy of the title of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — overall scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 1: Overall scientific and technical merits of the proposal and responsiveness to the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the degree of innovation and soundness of technical concept; awareness of the state of the art and scope of the problem (including technical risk); significance and originality of the technical approach; effort needed to address/solve the problem; anticipated impact within the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — facilities and capabilities of PI/key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 2: Overall facilities and capabilities of Principal Investigator and key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Offeror's facilities (extent to which the proposal reflects a coherent, coordinated collection of distributed facilities for research, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, workforce development) and qualifications, capabilities, and experience of the PI, team leader, and critical key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — organizational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 3: Overall organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes suitability of the organization for performing the work; academic and industrial partnership structure with well-defined royalty, licensing, and revenue methods; mechanisms and policies to ensure robust participation by small/medium businesses and large enterprises; well-structured and coherent IP management across contractual R&D arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — DoD relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 4: Potential relevance to the Department of Defense and contribution to a DoD component mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria — availability of funds / cost realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 5: The availability of funds, to include proposed cost share in the project. (Not applicable to white papers.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent appropriate, cost realism and reasonableness will be considered in selection. White papers: Criteria 1–4 are equally important. Full proposals: Criteria 1–5 are equally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection process characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted to a common work statement; ONR intends to review all proposals as soon as possible, but may review periodically for administrative reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate recommendation is made by ONR's scientific/technical community, then forwarded to Contracts and Grants for cost analysis, responsibility determination, fund availability, and other pre-award steps. Selection recommendation is not a guarantee of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award cybersecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, certain Offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance, or ability to comply, with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix 2, Section F, Administrative and National Policy Requirements for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting plan requirement (contracts > $750,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits (including educational institutions) must provide a Subcontracting Plan that contains all elements required by FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9, as supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are exempt. If an apparent successful Offeror fails to negotiate an acceptable Plan within the prescribed time, they will be ineligible for award. Plans are reviewed for adequacy and should propose realistic goals for small business participation; if SDB goals are below 5% an explanation of attempts to use small businesses is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to small business participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is strongly committed to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities to small businesses and socio-economic categories (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs, HBCUs/MIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should propose plans ensuring small businesses have the maximum practicable opportunity to participate consistent with efficient performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of current and pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of current and pending support made in the application may render an applicant ineligible for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD may request updated continuing and pending support information prior to award and throughout performance; updates will be reviewed and may result in discontinuation of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper electronic submission and FedConnect registration
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is utilizing FedConnect for submission of white papers; performers must register with SAM (UEI) and FedConnect to submit via FedConnect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for FedConnect registration and the FedConnect how-to guide are provided; first person registering must have SAM MPIN; FedConnect assistance contact provided; do not use FedConnect Message Center to submit questions—email POCs in Section G instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page/Cover Sheet requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cover Page is MANDATORY for white papers and must use the ONR-provided cover sheet for contract or grant submissions; FedConnect will not accept a white paper without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Program Officer’s information is a required field on the cover sheet; Cover Page links provided for contract and grant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and file-size limits for electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When email submission is required, white papers must be Microsoft Word 2016 or PDF compatible format and the email size limit is 5 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FedConnect and Grants.gov instructions for electronic submissions and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement on cooperation and IP expectations for teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data, and other information in an integrated program with other contractors and have coherent IP management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational structure and IP management are evaluation criteria; proposals should describe royalty/licensing/revenue methods and IP policies for collaborative environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation regarding covered telecommunications (Section 889)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Offeror must represent whether it will provide covered telecommunications equipment/services or uses such equipment/services; Section 889(a)(1)(A) and (B) prohibit certain procurements/contracting with entities that use covered telecommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Offeror responds 'will' or 'does', it must provide detailed disclosures about the covered equipment/services (manufacturer, model, use, PSC, etc.) as specified in the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remove impediments to award (responsibility and timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR reserves the right to remove Offerors from award consideration when parties fail to reach agreement on award terms, conditions, and cost/price within a reasonable time, or when the Offeror fails to timely provide requested or required additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus and scope guidance (technical fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of this BAA is primarily on projects that advance systems engineering approaches for design, fabrication, and manufacture of structural components addressing system weight, performance, affordability, and/or survivability, with emphasis on Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may include basic and applied research, technology/component development, prototyping, supply-chain technical support, workforce development, and manufacturing education. Potential Offerors are strongly encouraged to contact the ONR technical POC prior to preparing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit non-proprietary SOW and marking of proprietary pages
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must include a non-proprietary SOW. For proposals containing data the Offeror does not want disclosed, the title page must include a specific legend and each restricted sheet must be marked accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legend text and marking instructions are prescribed; the Government's right to use information obtained from other sources is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII purpose and expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs) bring together industry, non-profits, and academia with agencies to accelerate innovation by investing in industrially relevant manufacturing technologies (MRL 4–7) and provide shared access to state-of-the-art equipment; they propel R&D products to commercialization and economic viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIIs should support commercialization, workforce training, and become part of the DoD MII network.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII network design tenets
rubrics_metrics.description: MII design tenets include industry-driven public-private partnerships led by independent non-profits; federal funding matched by cost share; domestic industrial commons via shared IP/facilities; investments in applied/industry-relevant R&D; access for small/medium manufacturers; education and workforce investments; alignment with DoD/service modernization and commercial applications; sufficient size/scale for long-term economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — hire and retain key management staff
rubrics_metrics.description: MII management should be primarily focused on operation and management of the MII. Executive Director/CEO expected to be full-time and key management staff give >75% time commitment to the MII.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — establish and manage infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The MII should establish and operate physical and virtual infrastructure appropriate in scale and capability to the MII’s mission and leverage member-owned infrastructure; long-term operating costs should be covered by long-term revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — conduct annual planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ annual planning processes with broad stakeholder involvement; MII Annual Program Plan must include a detailed budget with a revenue strategy and plans to align business plan changes with the technology roadmap and federal partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop business plans for viability
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and implement business plans to become financially viable and world-leading, generate revenue, accelerate adoption of next-generation technologies, drive commercialization success, and attract continued investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — define structure and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: MII will operate under a non-profit but must be sufficiently independent and neutral in sub-award determinations and governance; should not compete with members for products/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — continuous improvement and technology roadmaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate lessons learned to widen impactful R&D while focusing on transformative value; periodically update integrated technology roadmaps and create mechanisms to assess progress towards goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — involve industry and academia
rubrics_metrics.description: Define clear by-laws, policies, and recruitment strategies to ensure active participation from a wide member base, leverage resources across sectors, and engage stakeholders along supply chain and regional economic organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — engage DoD and government partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop working relationships with government partners, accommodate DoD/government participation in decision-making bodies, and identify engagement opportunities to create investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop technology roadmap and project execution framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Create time-based and event-based roadmaps for maturing technology areas and demonstrate frameworks for defining, selecting, and executing projects addressing technology, manufacturing, workforce development, or demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — foster education and workforce development
rubrics_metrics.description: Support domestic technical workforce development through curricula, internships, co-ops, professional training, and re-training to bridge R&D to full-scale production and prepare students/trainees for workforce transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — develop manufacturing technology and prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the MII at cutting edge of applied research, ensure access to state-of-the-art equipment and expertise, and conduct R&D and prototyping to demonstrate future states for DoD and commercial customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — foster commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Target R&D investments toward projects, demonstrations, and prototypes intended to result in commercially successful products by industry partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — create and maintain an IP-protected innovation ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide collaboration on pre-competitive work in an IP-protected environment, foster inventor ownership of IP, protect background IP, and encourage commercialization through licensing and productization.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — coordinate industry standards development
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the MII to coordinate efforts with industry and Standards Development Organizations to identify needs for new/revised standards and accelerate their development.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — generate cost share and continued investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Attract cost share from members or stakeholders to sustain the MII, engage the ecosystem to stimulate continued investment in relevant technologies through the MII and the larger industrial base.

rubrics_metrics.name: MII critical function — enhance defense capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with DoD partners to include DoD modernization priorities and defense applications in the MII’s roadmaps; pursue technologies with both defense and commercial applications when they enhance defense capabilities.
